findings.what: The ladder stop rule conflicts with its own POSITIVE definition. L5(c) (and the RESUME POINT) says 'STOP when two consecutive rungs fail to beat the best display'. The four pre-scheduled blind rungs (39, 40, 41, exp70b) will most likely all display 0.954, the same as K2's best display, so the stop fires before any informed combo. Yet L5(a) says to submit the combination of POSITIVE knobs, and POSITIVE includes '0.954 plus an in-block move', which by definition does not beat the display. Neither text says which one wins, and the RESUME POINT repeats both.

findings.what: The insertion hedge has a hole. L9 eligibility caps runtime at L_hi <= 9.0 h, but the DaughterNet insertion is skipped in-kernel after DIVINS_DEADLINE_S = 28800 s (8.0 h). A V* with L_hi in (8.0, 9.0] h is therefore ELIGIBLE, yet it may carry NO insertion. The pair {V*, #38} would then hold two insertion-free files, which is exactly the failure the hedge exists to prevent, and L9(7) forbids the alternative {V*, #37}. The ledger already prints 'insertion gate 8.0 h: open/did NOT fire' for each ladder ref, but no rule reads it. Probability is low (K2 L in (7.36, 7.54] h), but #35 once had L_hi 7.73 h, and night queues vary.
